newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong 1997 investment in Shanghai seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong 1997 investment in Shanghai seen stable.

text.p: Hong Kong direct investment in Shanghai should remain at current levels through the handover of the territory back to China on July 1, a Hong Kong Trade Development Council official said on Tuesday.
But Wing Sham, director of the Shanghai office of the government-backed Hong Kong trade body, said longer-term prospects were uncertain.
China regains control of Hong Kong on July 1 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.

Official figures have ranked Hong Kong as the top source of foreign investment in Shanghai for the past few years. Contracted investment in the city by Hong Kong firms hit $3.86 billion in 1996, up 5.87 percent from 1995.
"I think 1997 should be roughly the same," Sham said in an interview. "The investment environment that I see this year is better than 1996 and 1995. After that I don't know."

He said he expected the property sector to continue to be the main focus of Hong Kong investment in China's largest city, followed by the service sector. Investment in manufacturing has declined in the past couple of years, he added.
